Wir sind das Digital Trendteam – eine spezialisierte B2B-Marketingagentur für CEO-Branding und Neukundengewinnung auf LinkedIn. Wir sorgen dafür, dass Geschäftsführer und Entscheider im Mittelstand digital sichtbar werden und planbar neue Kunden gewinnen.

Hinter unserem Wachstum steht eine klare Überzeugung:
Erstklassiger Vertrieb beginnt an der Front. Wir suchen keine Theoretiker oder Warm-Lead-Verwalter, sondern hungrige Vertriebstalente, die die Königsdisziplin im B2B-Sales beherrschen und lieben: Die Kaltakquise.

Bei uns erwartet dich ein leistungsorientiertes High-Performance-Umfeld, klare Prozesse und ein transparenter Karrierepfad vom Opener bis zum High-Ticket Closer.

Aufgaben

  • Aktive B2B-Kaltakquise (Outbound): Du greifst zum Hörer, wählst gezielt Geschäftsführer sowie Entscheider im Mittelstand an und weckst innerhalb der ersten Sekunden echtes Interesse an unseren Marketinglösungen.
  • Erstqualifizierung & Terminierung: Du identifizierst die Engpässe des Gegenübers, filterst unpassende Kontakte konsequent aus und terminierst qualifizierte Erstgespräche für unsere internen Setter.
  • Pipeline-Disziplin: Du steuerst deine täglichen Anwahlen fokussiert, hältst deine Kontakte lückenlos im CRM nach und sorgst für eine prall gefüllte Schlagzahl.
  • Prozesstreue: Du nutzt unser erprobtes Vertriebssystem, um mit hoher Schlagzahl und klarer Strategie deine wöchentlichen Ziele planbar zu erreichen.

Qualifikation

  • Bock auf Kaltakquise: Du weißt exakt, was B2B-Cold-Calling bedeutet. Ein "Nein" am Telefon wirft dich nicht aus der Bahn, sondern schärft deinen Fokus für das nächste Gespräch.
  • Biss & Schlagzahl: Du hast keine Angst vor dem Hörer und weißt, dass hohe Anwahlzahlen und mentale Stärke das Fundament für planbare Vertriebserfolge sind.
  • Kommunikationsstärke auf C-Level: Du sprichst selbstbewusst und auf Augenhöhe mit Entscheidern im Mittelstand – ohne verstellt oder abgelesen zu klingen.
  • Umsetzer-Mentalität: Du suchst keine Ausreden, sondern Ergebnisse. Du schätzt klare Vorgaben, setzt Feedback direkt um, statt zu diskutieren, und möchtest ein funktionierendes System auf höchstem Niveau exekutieren, anstatt jeden Tag das Rad neu zu erfinden.
  • Infrastruktur: Ein ruhiger Arbeitsplatz im Homeoffice, ein leistungsstarker Rechner und eine absolut stabile Internetverbindung sind vorhanden.

Benefits

  • Finanzielle Sicherheit: Unbefristeter Vollzeitvertrag in Festanstellung mit einem garantierten, planbaren Grundgehalt von 2.500 Euro – damit du dich voll auf deine Vertriebserfolge konzentrieren kannst.
  • Ungedeckeltes Provisionssystem: Ein hochattraktives und transparentes Vergütungsmodell mit pünktlicher Auszahlung. Wer bei uns Schlagzahl liefert und exzellent umsetzt, hat nach oben keine Grenzen.
  • Kaufbereiter Markt mit hoher Nachfrage: LinkedIn & B2B-Marketing sind Top-Themen im Mittelstand. Du verkaufst ein Produkt, das Unternehmen dringend brauchen.
  • 100% Remote & Flexibilität: Arbeite vollkommen selbstbestimmt aus dem Homeoffice – egal wo in Deutschland du dich befindest.
  • Intensives Mentoring & Coaching: Du wirst nicht alleine gelassen. Wir arbeiten dich intensiv ein und schulen dich kontinuierlich im B2B-Sales.
  • Klare Aufstiegschancen: Wer bei uns als Opener dauerhaft performt, hat die direkte Perspektive, zum Setter oder Closing-Berater aufzusteigen und Verantwortung im Vertriebsteam zu übernehmen.

Lass das Anschreiben weg. Sende uns einfach deinen Lebenslauf und eine kurze Info, welche Erfahrung du bisher in der Telefonakquise gesammelt hast.

Our client is a rapidly growing Australian company specialising in Property Education and Technology.Their mission is to help everyday Australians build wealth through education, strategic guidance, and innovative technology.

As they continue to grow, they're expanding their South African sales team and are looking for ambitious, career-focused professionals who want to develop world-class sales skills while working remotely for an international business.

This isn't just another appointment-setting role—it's an opportunity to build a long-term career in international sales.

Role Overview
As a Sales Development Representative (SDR), you'll be the first point of contact for Australians who have already expressed interest in learning more about property investing.

Working with warm enquiries, you will conduct structured qualification conversations, uncover each prospects goals, build rapport, and schedule appointments with one of the company's Senior Property Consultants.

You will be support by proven sales process, ongoing coaching, and a collaborative team that is invested in your success. If you are motivated by targets, enjoy speaking with people and want your earnings to reflect your performance, this role offers and exciting opportunity to grow.

Key Responsibilities

  • Engage with Australians who have already expressed interest in company's services.

  • Schedule qualified prospects into appointments with Senior Property Consultants
  • Follow up promptly with clients who miss or reschedule appointments.
  • Maintain accurate CRM notes and update customer records after every interaction.
  • Consistently achieve daily activity targets and weekly booking goals.
  • Participate in ongoing coaching, training, and performance development.

Requirements


We are looking for individuals who are ambitious, coachable, and genuinely enjoy speaking with people.

The ideal candidate will have:

  • Previous experience in sales, appointment setting, tele sales, customer service, or lead generation.
  • Excellent spoken and written English
  • A strong professional telephone manner.
  • A strong work ethic and desire to exceed targets.
  • The ability to work independantly from home.
  • Reliable internet and suitable home office environment.
  • Available to work 3:00am - 11:am SAST.

Experience selling into Australian market will be highly regarded but is not essentially.
Benefits

  • R18,000 per month base salary.
  • Realistic earnings of R34,000+ per month through uncapped commissions
  • Work exclusively with warm enquiries-no cold prospecting.
  • Work fully remote with flexibility of working from home.
  • Comprehensive onboarding and ongoing coaching from experienced Australian Sales Leaders.
  • Clear opportunities for career progression into senior sales and closing positions.
  • Join a supportive, high-performance culture that rewards effort, development, and results.
  • Gain valuable international sales experience with a growing Australian company

Who Thrives in This Role?


The people who perform best in this role aren't necessarily those with the most experience—they're the ones with the right mindset.You'll likely thrive if you:

  • Enjoy speaking with people and building genuine conversations.
  • Are naturally competitive and enjoy working towards goals.
  • Take ownership of your results rather than making excuses.
  • Are coachable and actively seek feedback to improve.
  • Stay positive and resilient, even after hearing "no."
  • Want your income to reflect your effort and performance.
  • Take pride in delivering an outstanding customer experience.
  • Are looking for a long-term career rather than just another remote job.

If you're the type of person who enjoys learning, embraces challenges, and gets satisfaction from achieving results, you'll fit right in with this team.We're looking for people who are hungry to grow, committed to continuous improvement, and excited by the opportunity to work with an ambitious Australian business.

raw.excerpt: Who We Are: Interra Health is a fast-growing healthcare technology company transforming how providers and patients navigate the prescription journey.
raw.description:
Who We Are:

Interra Health is a fast-growing healthcare technology company transforming how providers and patients navigate the prescription journey. Formed through the merger of DoseSpot, Arrive Health, and pVerify, Interra Health delivers trusted eligibility, real-time coverage and pricing insights, prescribing tools, and pharmacy transparency at the point of care—helping providers make informed decisions and patients access the right medications with greater clarity and affordability. Backed by strong market momentum and a bold vision for the future of connected care, Interra Health offers the chance to join an innovative, mission-driven team working at the intersection of software and healthcare to reduce friction, improve access, and make the healthcare experience better for everyone.

The Role:
Interra Health is looking for a Clinical Pharmacist to serve as the routine clinical point of contact across our product portfolio, bringing pharmacy and clinical credibility to the health systems, payers, PBMs, hubs, and pharma partners who depend on our platform. Sitting within Product and partnering with the Principal Clinical Specialist, you will be the clinical voice in customer engagements, the owner of clinical issue resolution, and the person who translates real-world clinical and workflow friction into a better product.

This is a hands-on, cross-functional role. You will move fluidly between client-facing working sessions and internal triage with Product, Engineering, Support, and QA — investigating clinical issues, validating fixes, and leading the clinical side of change management as releases ship — with deepest focus on network-partner integrations (EHR ↔ PBM) and the clinical exception paths that keep prescribing and pharmacy fulfillment running. The right person is a licensed pharmacist equally at home in a clinical exception queue and a customer business review, who brings clinical rigor, knows when to resolve and when to escalate, and treats every recurring issue as a signal to make the product better.

What You'll Do:
Clinical Engagement & Customer Support

  • Serve as the routine clinical point of contact for Interra Health customers and partners — health systems, payers, PBMs, hubs, and pharma — bringing clinical credibility to working sessions, business reviews, education initiatives, and client-facing conversations.

  • Partner with Strategic Accounts, Account Management, and Implementation teams to provide clinical fluency in customer engagements, escalating situational, senior, or strategic clinical conversations to the Principal Clinical Specialist.

  • Contribute to and review clinical content for customers and partners — presentation materials, educational resources, and tip sheets — ensuring accuracy, relevance, and alignment with stakeholder objectives.

  • Translate clinical and workflow friction points from customer engagements into product input, partnering with Product Managers to surface clinical requirements and improvement opportunities.

Clinical Issue Resolution & Change Management

  • Own clinical issue resolution across the product portfolio — triaging, investigating, and partnering with Product, Engineering, Support, and QA to drive resolution of clinical and clinical-workflow issues.

  • Document patterns in clinical escalations and recommend solutions that improve product reliability and reduce recurring clinical issues.

  • Lead the clinical aspects of change management — communicating changes that affect clinical workflows to internal teams and supporting customer-facing teams in cadence with releases.

  • Validate fixes, enhancements, and releases that affect clinical workflows or clinical content.

Clinical Domain Expertise

  • Apply pharmacy and clinical expertise across the portfolio, with deep focus on network-partner integrations (EHR ↔ PBM) and clinical exception support for prescribing and pharmacy fulfillment workflows.

  • Partner with the Principal Clinical Specialist on clinical quality standards, formulary integrity, and clinical decision support, applying those standards in day-to-day product, customer, and operational work.

Use SQL, dashboarding, and BI tools — alongside AI tools — to surface clinical trends, quantify new and recurring issues, and escalate clinical work for prioritization.

What You'll Bring:
Active pharmacist license in good standing, plus a minimum of 5 years of related experience as a pharmacist in a health system, health plan/PBM, or healthcare technology setting; or an equivalent combination of clinical practice and applied pharmacy experience.

  • Demonstrated understanding of medication order workflows from provider order entry through pharmacy adjudication and fulfillment.

  • Experience with formulary and benefit design, managed care principles, prior authorization, and clinical decision support.

  • Working proficiency in health data analysis using SQL, dashboarding, or BI tools (e.g., Tableau, Snowflake, Power BI) to investigate clinical client issues, identify trends, quantify issues, and represent the clinical voice of the customer.

  • Clinical informatics experience or exposure to health-data standards and analytics preferred (e.g., informatics coursework or certification, or hands-on work with clinical, pharmacy, or claims data sets).

  • Experience working with health systems, payers, PBMs, or healthcare technology vendors in a clinical or clinical-operations capacity.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present clinical content to product, engineering, and customer audiences.

  • Strong problem-solving and triage skills, with the ability to investigate clinical issues across complex product workflows.

Comfort operating in a fast-paced, post-merger SaaS environment where systems, priorities, and structures are still evolving.

Core Competencies:
Knowledge & Application

Applies solid pharmacy and clinical knowledge across the product portfolio, using established clinical standards and the Principal Clinical Specialist's guidance to support clinical workflows, exceptions, and content. Builds working depth in network-partner integrations (EHR ↔ PBM) and prescribing and pharmacy fulfillment workflows.

Complexity & Problem Solving

Resolves routine and moderately complex clinical and clinical-workflow issues using established methods, investigating and partnering across teams to drive resolution. Exercises sound judgment on day-to-day calls and escalates situational, senior, novel, or strategic matters to the Principal Clinical Specialist.

Collaboration & Interaction

Works effectively across Product, Engineering, Support, QA, Strategic Accounts, Account Management, and Implementation, and brings clinical credibility to conversations with external health systems, payers, PBMs, hubs, and pharma partners. Communicates clearly with clinical and non-clinical audiences and coordinates with the Principal Clinical Specialist on senior-facing engagements.

Pre-Employment Drug Screening: This position is subject to a pre-employment drug screening, where permitted by applicable law. Any required screening will be conducted after a conditional offer of employment and in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

Interra Health is an Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, protected veteran status, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Compensation Range: $120K - $155K

raw.excerpt: The PositionBallotpedia is seeking a full-time, 100% remote Donor Engagement Manager to join our External Relations team.
raw.description:
The Position

Ballotpedia is seeking a full-time, 100% remote Donor Engagement Manager to join our External Relations team.

Reporting to the Director of External Relations and working collaboratively with Ballotpedia’s External Relations team members and others across the organization, you will primarily focus on running many of Ballotpedia’s fundraising programs, including digital efforts and direct mail programs. You will build on Ballotpedia’s existing programs. You will grow Ballotpedia’s fundraising programs by turning readers and one-time givers into recurring members and repeat donors. This position will oversee the Ballotpedia Society membership program, the ad-free reader program, online giving, direct mail, donor retention communications, and seasonal fundraising campaigns.

The Donor Engagement Manager is a vital part of our fundraising team, and the role is perfect for someone who is an excellent fundraising writer, a curious and thoughtful analyst, and a reliable project manager. If you are a creative problem solver who enjoys designing experiments, analyzing results, and using what you learn to improve donor engagement, we want you on our team.

Responsibilities

As the Donor Engagement Manager, you will:

Donor Engagement and Fundraising

  • Manage and grow Ballotpedia’s membership and recurring giving programs, including Ballotpedia Society and the ad-free reader program.
  • Plan and execute membership pledge drives, direct mail appeals, Giving Tuesday, and 12 Days of Ballotpedia to meet annual fundraising goals.
  • Develop donor-centered fundraising copy and communications to attract new donors, retain existing supporters, and re-engage lapsed donors.
  • Execute and optimize testing strategies to improve online giving, donor conversion, and retention.
  • Coordinate mailing vendors, audience segmentation, and campaign schedules.
  • Identify and research promising donor prospects for follow-up by the Director of External Relations.
  • Oversee donor acknowledgments, gift processing, and payment issues.
  • Create regular reports and analyses on program performance, recommending growth opportunities and revenue goals.
  • Maintain donor data and campaign records in Salesforce, Classy, and WhatCounts.
  • Manage on-site advertising vendors and optimize advertising performance and revenue.

Cross-Departmental Collaboration

  • Partner with Communications, Tech, and Content to develop campaign materials and coordinate fundraising outreach and promotion.
  • Work with Tech to improve online giving and the ad-free donor experience.
  • Coordinate advertising revenue goals with the COO and ad placement improvements with Tech.

Skills and Qualifications

An ideal Donor Engagement Manager will:

  • Be a true believer in Ballotpedia’s mission to provide accurate, fact-based information to American voters. You’re excited about it and want to inspire others to support it.
  • Possess a strong customer service orientation and enthusiasm for creating a positive experience for Ballotpedia’s donors and members.
  • Demonstrate curiosity as a highly motivated self-starter, eager to understand what inspires donors to give and how to deepen their connection to Ballotpedia.
  • Bring a test-and-learn mindset, with enthusiasm for trying new approaches, analyzing results, and improving fundraising performance.
  • Exemplify “organized persistence” in keeping campaigns, donor communications, and recurring tasks on schedule.
  • Be effective at managing multiple projects with moving parts simultaneously and collaborating with colleagues and outside vendors.
  • Have strong research, written, and verbal communication skills, including the ability to write persuasive, donor-centered fundraising appeals.
  • Be comfortable working with data and spreadsheets to evaluate campaign results, identify trends, and recommend improvements.
  • Have experience in fundraising, donor engagement, membership programs, or related marketing work.
  • Be highly proficient with Salesforce (preferred) or other donor databases, with familiarity with online giving and email platforms such as Classy and WhatCounts.
  • Be receptive to feedback and eager to learn, adapt, and improve.

Environment

The Donor Engagement Manager will work remotely from their home location. All Ballotpedia staff work remotely. To join Ballotpedia, you must have a computer with Internet access.

Ballotpedia offers a flexible work environment, BP Flex, in which every employee enjoys unlimited vacation and flexible scheduling. Each employee will be oriented to the principles of Ballotpedia’s flexible environment during new employee training.

Compensation

The starting pay range for the Donor Engagement Manager is $60,000-$75,000/year, commensurate with experience.

In addition to salary, Ballotpedia offers an annual benefits stipend equivalent to $8,000 that is paid out in equal increments in each paycheck once an employee becomes benefits eligible. The stipend may be used to pay for a full benefits package, including health, vision, and dental insurance; retirement accounts; and more. If benefits are not elected, the stipend is taxed as regular income and added to salary.

To Apply

To apply, visit the Ballotpedia job opportunities page and fill out the form.

Please attach the following in PDF format:

  • Résumé
  • Cover letter detailing your interest in Ballotpedia’s mission and this position

Please ensure that either your résumé or your cover letter includes your current address.

Please note that if you are hired for this position, Ballotpedia participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S. If E-Verify cannot confirm that you are authorized to work, Ballotpedia is required to give you written instructions and an opportunity to contact the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) or Social Security Administration (SSA) so you can begin to resolve the issue before the employer can take any action against you, including terminating your employment. Employers can only use E-Verify once you have accepted a job offer and completed the Form I-9. For more information on E-Verify, or if you believe that your employer has violated its E-Verify responsibilities, please contact DHS.

About Ballotpedia
Ballotpedia is a mission-driven organization dedicated to providing Americans with accurate, relevant, and unbiased information about politics, elections, and public policy. Our mission is to ensure that the only unknown on your ballot is who gets your vote. We value innovation, humility, intellectual curiosity, drive, and a collaborative spirit and are committed to continuously improving our offerings to better serve our audiences, readers, and candidates.

Bocobay Group · Finance · Remote · Full-time · UK business hours

About Bocobay

Bocobay is a London-headquartered, high-growth hospitality and proptech company on a mission to become the go-to hospitality brand in the Caribbean. We combine proprietary technology with scaled local operations to run a luxury vacation rental portfolio of 400+ properties across Aruba, Curaçao, Jamaica and the Dominican Republic, with more islands on the way.

We're a lean, fast-moving, AI-first team. Finance sits at the centre of how we operate: multiple legal entities, homeowner associations, OTA channel payouts and owner statements, all run on a modern cloud stack (QuickBooks Online, Dext, Hostaway and our own Admin Portal). Two more entities join the Group in the next six months.

The Role

As Financial Controller, you'll own the accounting engine of the Group: bookkeeping quality, month-end close and reconciliations across all our operating subsidiaries and HOAs. You'll be the verification layer in our prepare–verify–oversee model, reviewing the work of our bookkeepers and making sure every set of books is clean, reconciled and locked on time.

You'll report to the Finance Director and work side by side with the Group Financial Controller. Between you, you'll keep a multi-island, multi-currency Group running on accurate numbers. You'll also play a key part in building finance from the ground up in our newest markets.

This role suits a mid-senior group accountant who enjoys bringing structure to complexity, likes being trusted with real ownership, and is comfortable working remotely within UK hours.

What You'll Do

Own the month-end close across the Group

  • Run bookkeeping and month-end for all operating subsidiaries (UK, Aruba, Curaçao, Jamaica, Dominican Republic) and our multiple homeowner associations (HOAs)
  • Perform full bank and balance-sheet reconciliations in QuickBooks Online every month, so each entity closes clean, on time and audit-ready
  • Post and review recurring and non-recurring journals
  • Close and lock QBO after each month end, and keep reopening tightly controlled with Finance Director sign-off

Be the quality gate for the finance team

  • Review and verify the work of our remote bookkeepers: invoice coding in Dext, payment instructions, bank uploads and draft journals
  • Champion our prepare–verify–oversee controls: segregation of duties, no payment without an approved invoice, and nobody approving their own work
  • Coach the team, spot recurring errors early and turn them into better processes

Steer tax, payroll and statutory compliance

  • Manage our outsourced local accountants for salary and tax calculations across the subsidiaries and HOAs, making sure every monthly filing and payment lands on time
  • Prepare annual accounts and statutory reporting for the HOAs, working with local auditors and advisers
  • Keep a clear compliance calendar across five tax regimes, so nothing slips

Partner the Finance Director

  • Provide clean, reliable numbers for management reporting, the monthly finance review and budgeting
  • Support HOA budget preparation and respond to finance queries from HOA boards and owners
  • Handle ad hoc requests from banks, payment providers and insurers, including KYC and reporting packs
  • Help shape a modern, AI-enabled finance function, automating the manual and documenting what works

What We're Looking For

  • Qualified or part-qualified accountant (ACCA, ACA, CIMA or European equivalent)
  • 5+ years in accounting, with at least 2 years at senior accountant, group accountant or assistant controller level
  • Hands-on experience running month-end close and balance-sheet reconciliations for a multi-entity, multi-currency group
  • Experience reviewing others' work and holding a team to a high standard
  • Strong working knowledge of QuickBooks Online or a similar cloud ledger (Xero, NetSuite, Sage Intacct)
  • Comfortable managing external accountants and advisers across several jurisdictions
  • Able to work UK business hours
  • Fluent written and spoken English
  • Organised, self-driven and calm under deadlines in a fully remote setting

Nice to have:

Deep Blue Recruitment is working with an international technology company looking to appoint an experienced Senior Privacy Counsel to join its legal team.

Operating in the enterprise technology sector, the business develops software and digital solutions for customers across a range of industries. With continued investment in emerging technologies, including AI, data protection is becoming an increasingly important consideration in how the business develops its products, manages risk and works with customers.

We're looking for a commercially minded privacy lawyer who enjoys working closely with the business, understanding how technology works and finding practical solutions to complex legal questions.

This is a broad, hands-on role combining privacy advisory work, commercial support and the continued development of internal data protection processes.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Advise colleagues across the business on a broad range of privacy and data protection matters, providing clear, commercially focused legal guidance.
  • Work closely with product, technology and commercial teams on the development of new services, ensuring privacy considerations are addressed early in the process.
  • Support the negotiation of commercial agreements, particularly around data processing, international transfers, customer relationships and third-party arrangements.
  • Advise on GDPR and other applicable international data protection regulations, helping the business understand and manage its obligations across different markets.
  • Provide legal guidance on emerging technologies, including AI, and the implications of new products and data processing activities from a privacy perspective.
  • Review and improve existing privacy policies, internal procedures and governance frameworks to ensure they remain practical and fit for purpose.
  • Work alongside information security and IT teams on data governance, risk assessments and privacy-related incidents.
  • Identify opportunities to improve the efficiency of privacy operations, including through automation and better internal processes.
  • Monitor regulatory developments affecting technology businesses, particularly around data protection, AI and digital services.
  • Provide training and guidance to colleagues across the organisation, helping non-legal teams understand their responsibilities when handling personal data.

What They're Looking For

  • A qualified lawyer with approximately 4-8 years experience specialising in data protection, privacy or technology law, gained in private practice, in-house or a combination of both.
  • Strong knowledge of GDPR and European data protection law, including regulatory guidance and its practical application within commercial organisations.
  • Experience advising technology businesses, ideally with exposure to software, AI, digital products or other data-intensive environments.
  • A good understanding of artificial intelligence technologies and the legal and regulatory challenges associated with their development and use.
  • Experience advising on commercial agreements involving personal data, international transfers and complex data processing arrangements.
  • Comfortable working directly with product, engineering and technical stakeholders, with the ability to understand complex issues and provide clear, practical legal advice.
  • A commercial approach to risk management, recognising that the role of legal is to help the business find workable solutions rather than simply identify problems.
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities independently.
  • Experience working within an international business or advising on privacy matters across multiple jurisdictions would be beneficial.

Why Consider This Opportunity?

This is an opportunity to join an international technology business where privacy plays an important role in how the company operates, develops its products and works with customers.

You'll have a broad remit, working closely with different teams across the organisation on a range of commercial, operational and regulatory matters, including some of the challenges emerging technologies bring to data protection.

If you're a privacy lawyer who enjoys working closely with the business, has an interest in technology and takes a practical approach to solving legal challenges, we'd be interested in hearing from you.

Job Title: Public Health Subject Matter Expert (Maternal and Child Health, Home Visiting)
Work Arrangement: Remote, with one or two in-person meetings in the Greater Boston area during the engagement
Location: Massachusetts (Greater Boston preferred)
Employment Type: Part-time contract, approximately 6 hours per week on average, November 2026 through June 2027
Engagement Type: 1099 Independent Contractor
Final Interview:

Position Summary

Dhaka Technologies Limited Company is hiring a Public Health Subject Matter Expert on behalf of a client, a Massachusetts regional public health collaborative that is designing and piloting a nurse-delivered home visiting program for new mothers and caregivers of young children. The Subject Matter Expert is the public health voice on a small consulting team. The team's project lead drafts the program design, pilot plan, learning questions, and family-facing materials; the Subject Matter Expert validates each of them against current public health practice and the evidence on home visiting, joins discovery sessions with municipal public health directors and nurses, and delivers short learning sessions for local public health staff who are new to early childhood work. This is an advisory and review role, not a service delivery role. Home visits are made by the client's own public health nurses.

Responsibilities

  • Review and validate the home visiting program design document, including the staffing model, referral sources, visit content, screening tools, and materials, against public health practice and the home visiting evidence base.
  • Review the short-term pilot plan and its learning questions, tracking approach, and learning cadence, and recommend changes before the pilot begins.
  • Review the plan and materials for engaging new mothers and caregivers directly, with attention to language access, trust, consent, and privacy.
  • Participate by video in discovery sessions with municipal public health directors and public health nurses, and in selected monthly coordination check-ins.
  • Review the landscape analysis of early childhood support groups for clinical and early childhood accuracy and completeness.
  • Design and deliver three to four learning sessions of 60 to 90 minutes for public health directors and staff on topics such as maternal, child, and family health within the Foundational Public Health Services framework, home visiting models and evidence, and closed-loop referral practice.
  • Present on the evidence and the pilot learning at one or two regional meetings, in person where scheduled.
  • Provide written review comments within agreed turnaround times and participate in the team's internal quality review of deliverables.

Required Qualifications

  • Doctorate (PhD, DrPH, or equivalent) in public health or a closely related field.
  • Experience working with Massachusetts local or regional public health departments, a Massachusetts public health shared services collaborative, or a Massachusetts Department of Public Health program within the last five years.
  • Experience designing, implementing, or evaluating maternal and child health initiatives, home visiting programs, or early childhood systems within the last five years.
  • Working knowledge of the Foundational Public Health Services framework as adopted in Massachusetts.
  • Ability to review program designs and plans critically and give clear, practical written feedback.
  • Experience facilitating or teaching sessions for public health practitioners.
  • Availability for about 6 hours per week on average from November 2026 through June 2027, with heavier involvement from November through January, and for one or two in-person meetings in the Greater Boston area.
  • Must be authorized to work in the United States without employer sponsorship, now or in the future.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Direct experience with a Massachusetts newborn or early childhood home visiting program, such as Welcome Family, Healthy Families Massachusetts, or a MIECHV-funded program.
  • Experience with closed-loop referral systems used in community health settings.
  • Experience advising municipal public health leadership or a multi-municipal collaborative.
  • Spanish, Portuguese, or Arabic language ability.

Compensation and Schedule

$40 to $50 per hour on a 1099 independent contractor basis, paid against approved monthly invoices. Approximately 210 hours over the engagement, averaging 6 hours per week, scheduled around the candidate's other commitments. Travel for the one or two in-person meetings is reimbursed.

How to Apply

Send a current resume or CV to with the subject line "Public Health Subject Matter Expert, Massachusetts." Please include two or three sentences describing your Massachusetts public health experience and your home visiting or maternal and child health work in the last five years.

About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role

We are looking for a Chief of Staff to help drive BJAK's AI Neobank expansion across products, markets and teams. This is a senior execution role for someone who can align leadership, drive operating cadence, solve cross-functional problems and turn strategy into measurable progress.

What You'll Own

  • Drive strategic execution across AI Neobank priorities. 

  • Build and manage operating rhythm, OKRs, leadership updates, decision tracking and accountability. 

  • Coordinate major workstreams across product, engineering, licensing, market expansion, partnerships, finance and operations. 

  • Prepare concise decision memos, board / leadership materials, execution plans and performance reviews. 

  • Identify gaps, risks and dependencies before they become serious blockers. 

  • Help leadership make sharper trade-offs on people, capital, product and market priorities. 

  • Own special projects that require senior judgement and cross-functional authority.


What We're Looking For 

  • Strong operator with experience driving strategic execution across teams. 

  • Excellent judgement, communication, prioritization and follow-through. 

  • Able to work with founders, CEOs, leadership teams and senior external stakeholders.

  • Comfortable operating in ambiguity with limited guidance. 

  • Can go from high-level strategy to detailed execution without losing quality. 

  • Strong writing, business analysis and problem-solving skills. 

  • Experience in startups, consulting, strategy, operations, fintech, financial services or regional expansion is a strong advantage.

The Kind of Builder We Want 

  • Makes the company move faster and with more clarity. 

  • Can challenge, align and unblock teams without adding bureaucracy. 

  • Stays close to facts, numbers, owners and deadlines. 

  • Balances strategic judgement with hands-on execution. 

  • Low ego, high ownership and strong bias for action.


This Role Is Not For

  • People who want a purely advisory role. 

  • Candidates who cannot handle pressure, ambiguity or senior accountability. 

  • People who create process without improving execution. 

  • Those who avoid operational details. 

  • People who prefer status over ownership.


Location

This role is based in United Kingdom. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our United Kingdom office at least 3 days per week.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

1. Online assessment or practical task

2. Technical interview

3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

Position Summary

Dhaka Technologies Limited Company is hiring a SNAP EBT Planning Consultant on behalf of its client, a state human services agency. The consultant will guide the agency through the re-procurement of its Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) services, from updating the EBT services RFP and preparing the federal Advance Planning Documents, through the evaluation of vendor responses, to acceptance testing of the new EBT system. The consultant will build and maintain the project timeline, keep every activity on track with U.S. Department of Agriculture, Food and Nutrition Service (USDA FNS) deadlines, and work closely with agency leadership, the state evaluation team, FNS and the EBT processor. The engagement is expected to run approximately 29 months, starting on or about January 1, 2027.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain the project timeline for the EBT re-procurement and make sure all activities meet USDA FNS deadlines.
  • Review the agency's SNAP EBT Services RFP and prepare updated drafts that address current federal requirements, including SNAP EBT regulations, FNS policy guidance and procedures, provisions of the Agricultural Act of 2018 and later amendments, and industry technical standards such as the Quest Operating Rules applicable to SNAP.
  • Research and document the state's business and technical requirements and build them into the RFP.
  • Take part in project calls with USDA FNS on the re-procurement RFP and the Advance Planning Document, and help the agency evaluate and implement FNS recommendations and changes.
  • Develop the plan the agency's team will use to evaluate RFP responses, including technical and cost evaluation criteria, the pricing evaluation structure, and scoring guidelines aligned with the state's statutory RFP evaluation criteria.
  • Prepare training materials, train the evaluation team on the evaluation tools (on site or virtually), and compile scores and summary documents that support the final award decision.
  • Develop and submit for FNS approval the Implementation Advance Planning Document (IAPD), and IAPD Updates (IAPDU) as needed, in line with the current FNS Handbook 901 and all applicable federal regulations. This includes the transmittal letter, executive summary, functional requirements, general system design, capacity study, project management plan and resource requirements, security planning, training plan, schedule of activities, milestones and deliverables, cost allocation plan, and proposed budget.
  • Prepare a comprehensive Test Plan, following FNS Handbook 901, Section 3.5.24, that defines the testing types (unit, integration, performance, end-to-end, user acceptance, regression and fail-safe testing), test team roles and responsibilities, test databases, test cases and scripts, the test schedule, acceptance testing procedures, Go/No-Go criteria, and contingency plans to revert to the legacy system.
  • Manage all testing processes and coordinate testing activities with the EBT processor to confirm the system meets program requirements, design specifications, performance standards, usability expectations, capacity demands and security requirements.
  • Lead System Acceptance Testing (SAT) covering functional requirements, security, recovery, system controls and what-if scenarios; prepare all SAT documents, scenarios and evaluation materials; review specifications, interface specifications and outputs; provide written comments; attend tests and test result walk-throughs; and take part in regression testing.
  • Train state staff to perform user acceptance testing.
  • Evaluate the overall completeness and results of testing, and prepare the written evaluation of test results for FNS review and approval.

Required Qualifications

  • 10 or more years of experience in consulting, program management or procurement for state human services, public benefits or health and human services information systems.
  • Direct experience with SNAP EBT (or WIC EBT) services for a state agency, including at least one EBT procurement, re-procurement or processor conversion.
  • Working knowledge of federal SNAP EBT requirements, including 7 CFR Part 274, FNS policy guidance, the Agricultural Act of 2018 and the Quest Operating Rules.
  • Experience preparing federal Advance Planning Documents (IAPD or IAPDU) under FNS Handbook 901, or comparable federal Advance Planning Documents for state human services systems.
  • Experience writing or rewriting state government RFPs and designing proposal evaluation criteria, scoring tools and evaluator training.
  • Experience leading system or user acceptance testing for a state system, including test plans, test scripts, Go/No-Go criteria and written evaluations of test results.
  • Excellent writing skills and the ability to produce clear, federally compliant documents.
  • No current employment with, or contract to, an EBT processor.
  • Available for the full engagement, starting on or about January 1, 2027.
  • Three professional references from previous engagements.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting an EBT processor transition, including card issuance, retailer integration and conversion planning.
  • Familiarity with eWIC, Summer EBT or other EBT-delivered benefit programs.
  • Experience working directly with FNS regional office staff.
  • Experience with state cost allocation plans and federal financial participation.
  • Experience with Medicaid Enterprise System (MMIS) procurements or CMS Advance Planning Documents.
  • Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.

How to Apply

Send your updated resume and three professional references (name, title, organization, phone number and email address) to with "SNAP EBT Planning Consultant" in the subject line. Please include your current location and your availability to start on or about January 1, 2027.

Adlib Software | North America, remote | Full time | Reports to the Chief Commercial Officer

About Adlib

Adlib is the document-to-decision engine for regulated industries. Our AI agents turn the documents and emails work arrives as into accurate, auditable decisions, with every value traced to its source. In September 2026 Adlib acquired Paperbox, the mail-to-decision engine for insurance, trusted by more than 100 European insurers. Together we serve a global customer base across insurance and other regulated industries, backed by Diversis Capital.

The role

We are hiring a VP, Global Marketing to lead marketing across North America and Europe. You will own marketing-sourced pipeline for insurance and marketing’s retention and expansion targets for our installed base, lead the brand through the next phase of the company’s evolution, and build the North American demand engine on a proven European playbook. You are quantitative and data driven: every program has a number, every dollar has a return. You will run an AI-powered marketing function, using the latest AI tools across content, campaigns, outbound and operations, and bring creative energy to a category where most vendors sound the same. You will lead a senior team spanning marketing operations, field marketing in North America and Europe, and GTM engineering, and partner closely with Sales, Product and Customer Success.

What you will do

  • Pipeline: own marketing-sourced pipeline, coverage and conversion targets for insurance, globally
  • Installed base: own marketing’s retention and expansion targets for customers outside insurance; customer, partner and lifecycle marketing that supports renewal and growth
  • North America: build the demand engine, field and event led, replicating the European playbook that won our first 100 insurers
  • Data driven: run marketing on the numbers; test, measure and reallocate spend to what converts
  • AI-powered marketing: run the function on the latest AI tools, including Claude and Regie.ai, across content, campaigns, outbound, account intelligence and reporting; more output per person, measured
  • Creative: bring distinctive ideas to campaigns, events and content; make Adlib and Paperbox the brands buyers remember
  • Brand: lead the global brand transition to an insurance-led, agentic company for regulated industries; land one brand architecture across Adlib and Paperbox and one web presence that serves every customer segment
  • Positioning: steward company and solution messaging; ensure consistent execution across regions, channels and sales enablement
  • Team and budget: lead and develop the global team; own the marketing budget and its return
  • Measurement: run one funnel from first touch to close; report pipeline, coverage, cost per opportunity, win rate and installed base results to the executive team and board monthly

What success looks like: first 90 days

  • Know the product: Adlib and Paperbox, what we sell, to whom, and why we win
  • Know the customers: time with insurance and installed base accounts, Sales and Customer Success
  • Know the funnel: what is working and what is not, by region, channel and program, with the data to prove it
  • Know the team: one global operating cadence across ops, field and GTM engineering
  • Deliver a diagnostic and a 12-month marketing plan to the executive team, with targets by quarter for insurance and the installed base
  • North American programs live on the proven European playbook
  • First creative ideas tested in market: one campaign, one event, one piece of content
  • AI operating model in place: tools, workflows and standards across the team
  • Funnel reporting in place: pipeline, coverage, cost per opportunity, win rate
  • Brand roadmap agreed with the executive team

What you bring

Required

  • 10+ years in B2B software marketing, 5+ leading teams
  • 5+ years of Insurance technology experience: carriers, MGAs, TPAs and their ecosystem
  • Scaled marketing at a growth-stage company ($15M to $40M ARR); PE-backed experience preferred
  • Quantitative and data driven: owned a pipeline number; fluent in funnel math, attribution, unit economics, marketing automation and Salesforce
  • Hands-on with AI tools across marketing, such as Claude and Regie.ai; has rebuilt workflows around them, not just trialed them
  • A portfolio of creative work that stood out in B2B and produced pipeline
  • Field and event led demand generation, hands-on
  • Marketed to an installed base across more than one industry
  • Led marketing across North America and Europe

Preferred

  • Launched a European product in North America, or replicated a playbook across regions
  • Led a rebrand or brand integration following an acquisition
  • Claims or underwriting domain knowledge

Location and travel

Remote in the United States or Canada. Travel about 25%, including industry events and our European offices.

Compensation and benefits

Base salary, annual bonus tied to pipeline and retention targets, equity, and a full benefits package.

Adlib is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every background and do not discriminate on any basis protected by law.

Accessibility and accommodation: Adlib is committed to an accessible, inclusive hiring process. Accommodations are available on request at every stage of recruitment, in line with the AODA and Ontario Human Rights Code in Canada and the ADA and applicable state and local laws in the U.S. To request an accommodation, contact .

AI in hiring

Adlib does not use artificial intelligence to screen, assess, or select applicants for this role.

Salary: $175,000-200,000 USD annually

Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.

As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually.

About the role

As a Principal Mobile Engineer (POS-Terminal) at Moniepoint, you will be responsible for designing and leading the architecture of our POS terminal solutions across multiple platforms. You will ensure the scalability, security, performance, and reliability of our POS systems and related applications, including mobile apps for repair scheduling and maintenance. While the majority of our terminals are currently based on Android Native, your expertise in cross-platform solutions (e.g., Flutter, C, JavaScript) will be crucial as we expand and diversify our portfolio.You’ll play a critical role in shaping the direction of our POS-related products, collaborating with cross-functional teams, and ensuring the technical vision aligns with the company’s broader strategic goals.

Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out posts on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth.

What you will do:

  • Lead the design and architecture of POS terminal solutions, ensuring security, scalability, performance, and integration with various hardware and payment systems.
  • Develop and maintain architectural documents and diagrams for POS terminal systems, ensuring all platforms are well documented and up to date.
  • Make architectural decisions on POS terminal software, integrating various payment technologies, EMV standards, and ensuring hardware compatibility.
  • Lead the development of POS-related applications
  • Optimize system performance and security, particularly around payment processing and EMV protocols.
  • Participate in planning sessions with product and engineering teams to ensure solutions meet market needs and business goals.
  • Conduct code reviews and ensure best practices for mobile and embedded systems development, especially for Android Native development.
  • Define and enforce software engineering best practices across the POS and related teams to improve efficiency and developer productivity.
  • Ensure the stability and reliability of POS terminal products and applications, monitoring system performance and troubleshooting as necessary.
  • Provide technical mentorship to engineering teams, helping them grow their skills and contribute to the broader technical vision.
  • Participate in the hiring process, screening engineers with expertise in POS systems, mobile, and embedded development.

To succeed in this role, we think you should have:

  • At least 8 years of experience in system design, architecture, and development, specifically in the POS terminal domain.
  • Strong expertise in Android Native development (Java/Kotlin), with a deep understanding of Android-based POS terminal solutions.
  • Experience in cross-platform mobile development, such as Flutter, and familiarity with other POS application platforms (e.g., C, JavaScript) is a plus.
  • Strong knowledge of EMV (Europay, Mastercard, and Visa) security protocols, including chip-based transactions, encryption, and key management.
  • Experience with hardware integration for POS devices, such as card readers, pin pads, printers, and other peripherals.
  • Deep understanding of payment systems architecture, including integration with payment processors and gateways.
  • Knowledge of software quality assurance principles and their application in financial systems.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills with an ability to manage complex system interactions and adapt to changing requirements.
  • Strong communication skills, capable of presenting complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Leadership abilities with a focus on mentoring engineers and driving process improvements within the team.

What we can offer you

  • Culture -We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We’ve built a company where all opinions carry weight and where all voices are heard. We value and respect each other and always look out for one another. Above all, we are human.
  • Learning - We have a learning and development-focused environment with an emphasis on knowledge sharing, training, and regular internal technical talks.
  • Compensation - You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance,annual bonus, plus other benefits.

What to expect in the hiring process

  • A preliminary phone call with one of our recruiters
  • A Takehome Hackerrank test.
  • A Technical interview session with our Engineering Team
  • A Technical and Behavioural Interview with our Head of Mobile Engineering
  • A Behavioral and Technical interview with a member of the Executive team.

About Venn

Venn is the leader in workspace security for remote and contractor workforces. Built on Venn's patented technology, Blue Border™ protects company data, applications, and AI workflows on any computer, without VDI and without fully managing the endpoint. Installing Blue Border creates a company-controlled secure enclave directly on the user's Mac or PC. All business activity, including data, applications, networking, and AI workflows, runs locally and stays isolated from personal use, while everything outside the enclave remains private.

Blue Border gives IT a simpler, device-agnostic way to secure remote work, enable contractor and BYOD workforces, govern AI usage, and replace VDI. More than 700 security and compliance-driven organizations, including Fidelity, Guardian, Whatnot, and the IMF, trust Venn to meet HIPAA, FINRA, SEC, NAIC, SOC 2, PCI, and GDPR standards.

The Opportunity

As the Revenue Operations Engineer at Venn, you'll make our go-to-market systems work as one. Our revenue stack spans HubSpot, Vitally, Nooks, Swan AI, Gong, and Zuora.You will own how those tools connect, how data flows between them, and how the business gets trustworthy reporting out of them. You'll sit in Finance and work daily with Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success, so that lead generation, pipeline, and customer data tie cleanly together from first touch through renewal. This is a hands-on, builder-minded role: you'll design integrations and automations, fix the data problems behind the numbers, and give leadership a single, reliable view of revenue.

What You'll Do

  • Own the integrations and data flows between our GTM systems, including HubSpot (CRM), Vitally (customer success), Nooks (AI phone dialer), Swan AI, Gong, and Zuora so that data moves accurately and automatically between them
  • Build and maintain automations and workflows that reduce manual work for Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success teams
  • Serve as the technical owner of HubSpot, including objects, properties, workflows, lead routing, lifecycle stages, and data hygiene
  • Design and maintain reporting and dashboards for pipeline generation, conversion, sales activity, forecasting, and customer health, working with Finance on revenue reporting
  • Define and document metrics and data definitions so Sales, Marketing, CS, and Finance all work from the same numbers
  • Partner with Marketing on lead flow, attribution, and campaign reporting from first touch through closed-won
  • Partner with Sales leadership on pipeline visibility, forecast inputs, and rep productivity reporting
  • Partner with Customer Success on connecting customer health, usage, and renewal data to the CRM
  • Audit data quality across systems, find and fix sync errors, duplicates, and gaps, and put safeguards in place to prevent them
  • Evaluate new GTM tools and AI-driven workflows, and manage vendor setup, permissions, and integrations
  • Document systems, processes, and integrations so the revenue stack is easy to maintain and scale
  • Support Finance with revenue, bookings, and pipeline data for board reporting, planning, and audits

What You Bring

  • 3-5 years of experience in revenue operations, GTM operations, marketing operations, sales operations, or a similar technical GTM role, ideally at a B2B SaaS company
  • Deep, hands-on experience with HubSpot, including workflows, custom properties and objects, reporting, and integrations
  • You know the Model Context Protocol (MCP). You can connect AI tools to business systems with MCP connectors (for example, HubSpot, Zuora, and Google Drive)
  • Experience connecting systems and building integrations through native connectors, APIs, webhooks, and iPaaS tools (e.g., Zapier, Workato, Make, n8n, or similar)
  • Strong reporting and analytics skills, with experience building dashboards and translating messy data into clear answers for leadership
  • Familiarity with the types of tools in our stack, such as customer success platforms, sales dialers and engagement tools, and conversation intelligence platforms (Vitally, Nooks, and Gong experience is a plus)
  • Comfort working across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and Finance, and explaining technical concepts to non-technical teammates
  • A detail-oriented, systems-thinking approach, with a habit of documenting what you build
  • Strong problem-solving instincts and the ability to prioritize competing requests from multiple stakeholders
  • Comfort in a startup or scale-up environment, with a bias toward action and a willingness to build process as you go

Nice to Have

  • Working knowledge of SQL, JavaScript or Python, or scripting for data transformation and API work
  • Experience with BI or data tools (e.g., Looker, Tableau, Metabase, Google Sheets or BigQuery modeling)
  • Experience supporting finance reporting, such as bookings, ARR, and revenue recognition inputs
  • Experience with AI-driven GTM tools and automation
  • HubSpot certifications

Why You'll Love Working Here

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support our team's health, well-being, and work-life balance, including:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance
  • Healthcare FSA, HSA, and commuter benefits
  • Unlimited paid time off, paid sick time, NYSE company holidays, and a paid birthday off
  • The opportunity to be part of a fast-growing startup with a collaborative, high-impact team where every voice is valued and there are clear paths for growth and promotion

We operate with Trust, Humility, Relationships, Innovation, Vigor, and Empowerment, and we look for teammates who do the same.

Overview

Remote Registered Nurse (RN) – DH Direct Triage

Part-Time, 20 hours per week

Position Summary

The RN - DH Direct Triage provides high-quality, patient-centered care through telephone triage and clinical assessment. This role is 100% hands-on, responsible for assessing patient symptoms, determining the appropriate level of care, providing education, and ensuring timely communication with providers. The ideal candidate has strong triage, Med-Surg, and Primary Care experience, is proficient with Epic EMR, and thrives in an independent remote environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform telephone triage using established protocols and sound nursing judgment.
  • Assess symptoms, prioritize patient needs, and determine appropriate care or follow-up.
  • Provide patient education, guidance, and reassurance as appropriate.
  • Accurately document all patient encounters in Epic EMR in real time.
  • Escalate urgent or emergent situations per clinic and organizational policies.
  • Communicate effectively with on-call providers, clinic teams, and patients to ensure continuity of care.
  • Contribute to a culture of safety, quality, and patient satisfaction within the triage team.

Qualifications Required:

  • Active, unrestricted RN license (multi-state compact required).
  • Minimum 2-3 years of clinical experience with a strong background in triage, ER, and/or Primary Care.
  • Proficiency in Epic EMR and remote communication systems.
  • Excellent assessment, critical thinking, and decision-making skills.
  • Strong communication, documentation, and time management abilities.
  • Self-motivated and comfortable working independently in a remote environment.

Preferred:

  • Associates degree required; BSN preferred
  • Previous experience in remote triage, nurse advice lines, or outpatient/clinic settings.

Schedule & Work Environment

  • Evenings with weekends and a holiday rotation
  • 100% remote position — requires reliable internet and a secure HIPAA-compliant workspace, free from distractions.

* Eligible candidates will reside in one of the following compact eligible states: Arizona, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Indiana, Kentucky, Maine, Maryland, New Hampshire, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington.

These are just a few highlights of being a nurse at Dartmouth Hitchcock Medical Center and Clinics in New Hampshire.

  • We have loan repayment up to $20,000.
  • We offer Relocation Assistance and a Housing Coordinator to take on the burden of finding a home.
  • We offer generous tuition reimbursement.
  • We have a very popular "earned time" plan.
  • We have extensive CEU/Training programs.
  • Our 8,000 ft Patient Safety and Training Simulation Center is state-of-the-art.
  • Our nurses serve as central figures in the success of our system through our shared governance nursing model.
  • We offer a rigorous, research-focused environment.
  • Dartmouth Hitchcock's Nursing Continuing Education Council is accredited as a provider of continuing nursing. education by the American Nurses Credentialing Center.

Read more about Dartmouth Health and why YOU should work here.

The Dartmouth Health system stretches over New Hampshire and Vermont and offers the quintessential New England experience. With no income or sales tax, this beautiful area combines history, industry, and business and has been ranked consistently as one of the best places in the US to live and work. Anchored by the academic Dartmouth Hitchcock Medical Center in Lebanon, NH, the system includes the NCI-designated Dartmouth Cancer Center, Dartmouth Health Children’s; member hospitals, and 30 Dartmouth Hitchcock ambulatory clinics across the region. With destinations like Boston, New York, the seacoast, and ski country within driving distance, the opportunities - both career and personal - truly make New Hampshire the ideal place to work and play.

Applicants are encouraged to visit our nursing career site to learn more and apply:

Please visit:

Dartmouth Health is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, veteran status, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Responsibilities

The Clinical Nurse is an engaged and credentialed member of the Professional Nursing Organization and is responsible for autonomous practice directed by the professional tenets of practitioner, leader/decision maker, scientist and transferor. The Clinical Nurse is responsible for utilizing the nursing process to provide evidence-based care and to continuously monitor and evaluate practice to ensure safe passage of patients that is in the best interest of populations served.

Practitioner

  • Utilizes the nursing process to assess, diagnose, identify outcomes, plan, implement and evaluate an individualized plan of care.
  • Utilizes critical thinking and the nursing process to anticipate and recognize changes in patient status, taking action to modify the plan of care or to elevate to the care team as necessary.
  • Practices in accordance with the ANA Code of Ethics to advocate for patients, uphold their autonomy in decision-making, ensure informed consent and assist patients in families in expressing self-determination.
  • Actively seeks feedback and acts to improve performance.
  • Engages in the governance of practice.

    • Leader/Decision Maker

  • Manages interpersonal relationships for self and with others.
  • Mentors colleagues for the advancement of nursing practice and the profession.
  • Assumes authority and accountability for the nursing care of patients while appropriately delegating elements of care to others members of the care delivery team in accordance with laws, regulations and policies and procedures.
  • Prioritizes and organizes time to optimize patient outcomes.

    • Scientist

  • Actively seeks out the most current evidence and standards and applies and translates to daily practice.
  • Role models a culture of inquiry, developing new knowledge by contributing to research, quality improvement, and evidence-based practice at the local level.

    • Transferor

  • Communicates effectively in a variety of formats in all areas of practice.
  • Actively partners with others to effect change that produces positive outcomes through the exchange of knowledge.
  • Precepts the student nurse, nurse extern, nurse resident, experienced clinical nurse and other members of the healthcare team.
  • Performs other duties as required or assigned.

    • Qualifications

    • Graduate from an accredited Nursing Program required.
    • Bachelor of Science Degree in Nursing (BSN) preferred.

    Required Licensure/Certifications

    • Licensed Registered Nurse with NH eligibility
    • Basic Life Support (BLS) Certificate required upon hire.

PERSUIT is a leading legal technology company transforming how in-house legal teams engage outside counsel and manage legal spend. Our innovative platform helps some of the world's largest organizations make smarter, more strategic decisions through competitive sourcing, greater transparency, and data-driven insights. We're a collaborative, fast-growing team passionate about challenging the status quo and driving meaningful change across the legal industry.

As a Customer Success Manager at PERSUIT, you'll partner with in-house legal teams to transform how they select and manage outside counsel and control legal spend, from intake to invoice.

You'll own a portfolio of North American enterprise clients and act as a strategic advisor to General Counsel and Legal Operations leaders. Your goal is to deliver measurable value, build lasting client relationships, and make renewal a no-brainer.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Own a portfolio of enterprise clients across the full customer lifecycle, including onboarding, adoption, expansion, and renewal.
  • Build data-driven success plans and advise clients on outside counsel management best practices, including competitive sourcing, alternative fee arrangements, and spend governance.
  • Turn usage and savings data into a clear value story that drives renewal and expansion.
  • Build executive sponsorship and develop strong, multi-threaded relationships across every account.
  • Drive adoption through training, change management, and scalable self-service programs.
  • Identify risks and growth opportunities early, collaborating with the right internal experts to take action.

This is a fully remote position open to candidates based in the United States. While we welcome applicants nationwide, candidates located in the Eastern, Central, or Mountain time zones are preferred.

We're AI-friendly. Feel free to use tools like ChatGPT during your prep, but we ask that your interview responses and work samples reflect your own thinking.

  • Confident engaging with senior stakeholders and comfortable leading high-stakes conversations.
  • A data-literate storyteller who can translate complex information into clear, actionable insights.
  • Proactive, organized, and technically curious, with an interest in leveraging technology and AI to work smarter.

PERSUIT offers a comprehensive benefits package, including:

raw.description:
Position Summary

The Epilepsy Foundation is seeking a detail-oriented and strategic Senior Manager of Contracts and Procurement with deep experience in government grant compliance, contract negotiation, procurement, and regulatory reporting within the nonprofit sector.

This role is responsible for overseeing the organization’s contracts and procurement functions while ensuring compliance with federal, state, and local requirements, including the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act (FFATA), Uniform Guidance (2 CFR Part 200), and applicable state charitable registration requirements.

The ideal candidate will have demonstrated experience navigating complex regulatory requirements, managing high-stakes contracts and agreements, and partnering across departments to mitigate organizational risk and ensure compliance. This position will serve as a key subject matter expert on grant-related procurement, contracting, and regulatory obligations while supporting the Foundation’s mission and organizational priorities.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Contracts & Procurement Management: Execute and oversee the end-to-end contracts and procurement function, with a strong focus on regulatory compliance for federally and state-funded grants.
  • Federal Grant Compliance: Ensure organizational adherence to federal grant requirements, including FFATA reporting, Uniform Guidance (2 CFR Part 200), cost principles, procurement standards, and other applicable requirements.
  • Contract Development & Negotiation: Lead the review, drafting, negotiation, and administration of contracts, memoranda of understanding (MOUs), subrecipient agreements, cooperative agreements, and vendor contracts.
  • Charitable Registration Compliance: Coordinate state charitable solicitation registrations, renewals, and related compliance requirements across applicable jurisdictions.
  • Policies & Procedures: Develop, implement, maintain, and continuously improve procurement and contracting policies and procedures that align with nonprofit best practices and regulatory requirements.
  • Grant & Funder Requirements: Monitor and report on compliance with funder-specific procurement requirements, contractual obligations, and reporting requirements.
  • Subject Matter Expertise: Serve as the organization’s subject matter expert on grant-related procurement, contracting requirements, and regulatory obligations.
  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Partner closely with Legal, Finance, Programs, Development, and other internal stakeholders to align procurement and contracting activities with organizational goals, grant requirements, and deliverables.
  • Vendor & Subcontractor Management: Manage supplier, vendor, subcontractor, and subrecipient due diligence, contractual obligations, compliance requirements, and performance.
  • Audit Support: Play an integral role in organizational audits, including the annual Uniform Guidance Audit, by ensuring appropriate procurement and contracting documentation and compliance.
  • Training & Guidance: Develop and provide training and guidance to internal stakeholders on procurement compliance, contracting procedures, ethics, and federal and state funding requirements.
  • Risk Management: Identify and mitigate contractual, procurement, and compliance risks while ensuring appropriate documentation and internal controls.
  • Process Improvement: Identify opportunities to strengthen contracting and procurement processes, improve operational efficiency, and enhance organizational compliance.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Law, Public Administration, Business Administration, Finance, or a related field required; JD or master’s degree preferred.
  • Minimum of 8–10 years of progressive experience in contract management and procurement, including at least 5 years supporting federal and state grant compliance within a nonprofit, government, or government-funded environment.
  • In-depth knowledge of FFATA, 2 CFR Part 200 (Uniform Guidance), federal procurement requirements, cost principles, and state charitable registration requirements.
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex grant-related contracts, subrecipient agreements, cooperative agreements, subcontracts, and vendor relationships.
  • Strong contract drafting, review, negotiation, and risk assessment skills.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of procurement regulations, internal controls, audit readiness, and compliance requirements applicable to nonprofits and federal grantees.
  • Experience supporting organizational audits, including Uniform Guidance Audits.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, problem-solving, and project management skills.
  • Ability to interpret complex regulatory and contractual requirements and communicate them clearly to internal stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively across Legal, Finance, Programs, Development, and other organizational functions.
  • Ability to manage multiple complex priorities and deadlines while maintaining strong attention to detail.
  • Demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgment, discretion, and ethical decision-making.
  • Proficiency with contract, grant, financial, and organizational management systems; experience with Salesforce and Sage Intacct preferred.

Key Competencies:

  • Regulatory & Compliance Expertise
  • Contract Drafting & Negotiation
  • Federal & State Grant Compliance
  • Nonprofit Legal & Regulatory Acumen
  • Procurement & Vendor Management
  • Risk Assessment & Mitigation
  • Attention to Detail
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Strategic Thinking & Process Improvement
  • Ethical & Transparent Decision-Making

Travel & Work Requirements:

  • This is a remote position with travel required approximately 4–6 times annually for organizational meetings, conferences, audits, trainings, or other business-related activities.
  • Must be able to work effectively and collaboratively in a remote work environment.
  • Occasional flexibility outside of standard business hours may be required to support audits, reporting deadlines, contract negotiations, or other time-sensitive organizational needs.
